CLAIMS WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A system comprising: a pressure-sensing device comprising: a device frame comprising a base surface and a frame attachment region, wherein the base surface is configured to rest on an external supporting structure that is separate from the pressure-sensing device, and wherein the frame attachment region is located opposite to the base surface such that the frame attachment region is raised from the external supporting structure when the base surface is resting on the external supporting structure; a flexible membrane including a membrane attachment region attached to the frame attachment region, wherein the flexible membrane protrudes above the device frame and is configured to conform to a user's perineum region when the user is seated on the flexible membrane, and wherein the device frame and the flexible membrane at least partially enclose a pressure chamber including an air mass between the device frame and the flexible membrane; a pressure sensor at least partially included within the pressure chamber and in contact with the air mass, the pressure sensor configured to generate a pressure signal indicating air pressure of the air mass in the pressure chamber caused by user muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region; and device electronics in communication with the pressure sensor, wherein the device electronics are configured to: determine the air pressure in the pressure chamber based on the pressure signal; and
transmit pressure data to a user computing device indicating the determined air pressure, wherein the pressure data indicates changes in the determined air pressure caused by user muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region; and a non-transitory computer-readable medium comprising computer-executable instructions configured to cause the user computing device to render a graphical user interface (GUI) that includes one or more GUI elements that are controlled based on received pressure data.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more GUI elements indicate at least one of a user contraction strength and a number of contractions.
3. The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more GUI elements prompt the user to perform at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
4. The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more GUI elements include one or more rendered shapes.
5. The system of claim 4, wherein the one or more rendered shapes are controlled based on the received pressure data.
6. The system of claim 5, wherein the one or more rendered shapes are moved in the GUI based on the received pressure data.
7. The system of claim 4, wherein the one or more rendered shapes prompt the user to perform at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
8. The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more GUI elements include a game character.
9. The system of claim 8, wherein the game character is controlled based on the received pressure data.
10. The system of claim 9, wherein the game character is moved in the GUI based on the received pressure data.
11. The system of claim 8, wherein the one or more GUI elements prompt the user to control the game character by performing at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
12. The system of claim 1, wherein the computer-executable instructions are configured to cause the user computing device to prompt the user to perform muscle contractions in the perineum region according to interactive audible feedback.
13. A system comprising: a pressure-sensing device comprising: a device frame comprising: a base surface configured to rest on an external supporting structure that is separate from the pressure-sensing device; a frame attachment region located opposite to the base surface such that the frame attachment region is raised from the external supporting structure when the base surface is resting on the external supporting structure; and a seating surface;
a flexible membrane comprising a membrane attachment region attached to the frame attachment region, wherein the device frame and the flexible membrane at least partially enclose a pressure chamber between the device frame and the flexible membrane, wherein the pressure chamber includes an air mass, wherein the seating surface extends outward around the flexible membrane, wherein the flexible membrane protrudes above the seating surface and is configured to conform to a user’s perineum region when the user is seated on the flexible membrane and the seating surface, and wherein the seating surface is configured to contact a portion of the user around the flexible membrane; a pressure sensor at least partially included within the pressure chamber and in contact with the air mass, the pressure sensor configured to generate a pressure signal indicating air pressure of the air mass in the pressure chamber caused by user muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region; and device electronics in communication with the pressure sensor, wherein the device electronics are configured to: determine the air pressure in the pressure chamber based on the pressure signal; and transmit pressure data to a user computing device indicating the determined air pressure, wherein the pressure data indicates changes in the determined air pressure caused by user muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region; and a non-transitory computer-readable medium comprising computer-executable instructions configured to cause the user computing device to render a graphical user interface (GUI) that includes one or more GUI elements that are controlled based on received pressure data.
14. The system of claim 13, wherein the one or more GUI elements indicate at least one of a user contraction strength and a number of contractions.
15. The system of claim 13, wherein the one or more GUI elements prompt the user to perform at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
16. The system of claim 13, wherein the one or more GUI elements include one or more rendered shapes.
17. The system of claim 16, wherein the one or more rendered shapes are controlled based on the received pressure data.
18. The system of claim 17, wherein the one or more rendered shapes are moved in the GUI based on the received pressure data.
19. The system of claim 16, wherein the one or more rendered shapes prompt the user to perform at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
20. The system of claim 13, wherein the one or more GUI elements include a game character.
21. The system of claim 20, wherein the game character is controlled based on the received pressure data.
22. The system of claim 21, wherein the game character is moved in the GUI based on the received pressure data.
23. The system of claim 20, wherein the one or more GUI elements prompt the user to control the game character by performing at least one of muscle contractions and muscle relaxations in the perineum region.
24. The system of claim 13, wherein the computer-executable instructions are configured to cause the user computing device to prompt the user to perform muscle contractions in the perineum region according to interactive audible feedback.
